policy.name: XAU_DIRECTIONAL_CONFIRMATION_V1
notes: The candidate family is frozen to the Phase I-D robust survivors whose outcome is mean_fwd_ret_atr. The much larger move_ge_1atr family is classified as non-directional movement/volatility behavior and is not eligible for directional alpha promotion.
No state, feature, quintile cutpoint, hour block, outcome, horizon, target, stop, sizing, cost, or PnL parameter may be created or retuned in this phase.

All 2024-fitted Phase I-C cutpoints remain frozen. Phase I-E reuses only 2025 and is a stricter multiplicity/autocorrelation/redundancy confirmation of already frozen Phase I-D directional candidates; 2026 is forbidden.

Each eligible candidate must retain the Phase I-D sign and at least 0.06 ATR state-vs-complement mean forward-return effect over full 2025, and independently in every 2025 calendar quarter with at least 100 state observations per quarter.
Full-2025 normal-approximation p-values are controlled across the entire frozen eligible family with Holm family-wise alpha 0.05.

A contiguous moving-block bootstrap over 2025 rows, block length 24 M5 bars and 5000 deterministic replicates, preserves state/outcome temporal dependence. Its two-sided Bonferroni familywise confidence interval must exclude zero in the frozen effect direction.

Signal-mask redundancy is measured after statistical testing. Passing candidates with 2025 Jaccard overlap >=0.90 and the same effect sign are clustered; the canonical representative is chosen lexicographically, never by realized effect size.

A Phase I-E survivor cluster is still a frozen phenomenon candidate, not a strategy and not prop-firm authorization. If at least one independent directional cluster survives, the supervisor must commit an exact protected-2026 preregistration and obtain explicit owner approval before opening 2026. If none survives, close the XAU directional family rather than rescue it with sizing or Challenge Lab.
